supersedes.rule: Legacy PR/G artifacts may be retained only as historical evidence and must never be used to resolve current work, current phase, writable scope, or acceptance state.

scope.objective: Converge LocalBridge onto a control-plane architecture with single mutable ownership per authoritative fact, explicit identities and lifecycles, explicit scheduling, Desired/Observed/Effective convergence, revisioned UI snapshots, typed errors, and transport/domain separation.
root_causes: No explicit unique mutable owner for authoritative facts
No explicit Scheduler; Mutex currently performs implicit serialization
Projection and Error are not first-class control-plane state
scope.core_principle: Every authoritative fact has exactly one mutable owner.

architecture.control_plane: typed API shared by MCP and Tauri transports
architecture.reconciler: converges observed state toward desired state

rules: Raw JSON-RPC id alone is never an internal request identity
Every Task has a stable TaskId
Every real execution attempt has a distinct ExecutionId
Only detached executions receive a PublicSessionId
ConnectionId is diagnostics-only and never business identity
ClientId is not introduced unless future cross-session stable client identity is required

request_registry.required_storage: HashMap<RequestKey, ActiveRequest> or semantically equivalent keyed registry

with_task_id.scope: current MCP session plus specified TaskId

delete_policy: detach or retain durable/detached resources according to explicit lifecycle policy
session_lifecycle.capacity_rule: reap expired sessions before evaluating MAX_DOWNSTREAM_MCP_SESSIONS

snapshot.publication: mutation -> derive snapshot -> revision += 1 -> wake UI

classes.OperationError: transient user operation result; presentation may use Toast
classes.PersistentFault: owned by backend control plane and present in snapshot.active_faults until actual recovery

module_boundaries.mcp_final_role: MCP request -> typed Intent -> ControlPlane -> typed Result -> MCP response

R1.title: Identity / Isolation
R1.goal: Eliminate cross-MCP-session request collision and cancellation cross-talk P0.
required_outcomes: Replace all bare request-id active/cancellation registries with RequestKey-scoped ownership
Prove same JSON-RPC id in distinct MCP sessions is isolated

R2.title: Task / Execution Convergence
R2.goal: Converge lifecycle and eliminate single-slot command truth and terminal projection divergence.

R3.title: Explicit Scheduler + Session Lifecycle
R3.goal: Turn multi-window/multi-session work into explicit bounded queueing and bounded session lifecycle instead of busy/502/503 behavior.

R4.title: Desired / Observed Convergence
R4.goal: Replace manual synchronization and rollback compensation with reconciled Desired/Observed/Effective state.

R5.title: Snapshot / Typed UI
R5.goal: Make projection and error first-class revisioned control-plane state.

R6.title: Boundary Cleanup
R6.goal: Complete transport/domain separation after ownership and snapshot migration are stable.
required_outcomes: MCP module reduced to protocol, transport, and mapping
Structured filesystem authorization separated from shell execution policy
All workspace paths resolved through WorkspaceResolver
Dependency direction is transport -> control_plane -> domain/runtime/privilege/workspace

R7.title: Product Lifecycle
R7.goal: Add bounded update and release-discovery lifecycle on top of the converged control plane.
required_outcomes: Update checker has one typed owner and explicit lifecycle
GitHub release link and version detection are typed and observable
Startup update check is bounded, retryable, and cannot block runtime readiness
Update state is published through the revisioned snapshot and typed UI boundary

invariants.INV-01: Every authoritative fact has exactly one mutable owner.
invariants.INV-02: Every request identity is scoped by MCP session.
invariants.INV-03: Every Task and Execution has stable identity and exactly one terminal outcome.
invariants.INV-04: Cancellation may only affect resources owned by its declared scope.
invariants.INV-05: Accepted Work must be explicitly Queued, Running or Terminal; implicit Mutex waiting is not task state.
invariants.INV-06: UI snapshots are published under one revision; fabricated business state on lock contention is forbidden.
invariants.INV-07: Every runtime resource type has an explicit bounded lifecycle and reaping policy.
invariants.INV-08: Desired, Observed and Effective state are distinct; Effective authority/workspace is derived fail-closed.
invariants.INV-09: Transport layers cannot own domain lifecycle state.

required_adversarial_tests: Session A request id=1 and Session B request id=1 are independent
Cancelling Session A request 1 does not affect Session B request 1
A/B/C MCP sessions submit work concurrently and receive explicit queue semantics rather than busy errors
Detached A remains running while short B completes; projection never leaves B falsely running and restores A
task_control(cancel) can cancel only the caller session's owned task
Session DELETE terminals transient owned resources and applies explicit detached/durable policy
Abnormal client exit is eventually reaped by TTL
Every accepted Task reaches exactly one terminal outcome
Runtime restart maps unfinished Execution to Lost instead of permanent Running
Lock contention produces stale/unavailable, never fabricated Running
CredentialStore fault does not blind Runtime/Task/Broker projection
Desired Elevated plus Broker Offline yields configured Elevated, effective non-elevated, observable reconciliation
Desired workspace B plus observed workspace A yields fail-closed execution authority
All sections of Snapshot revision N are derived from the same revision

feature_freeze.filesystem_policy: bug fixes only; do not expand responsibility during R1-R3

final_completion_criteria: Every Request has a unique RequestKey
Every Task has a unique TaskId
Every Execution has a unique ExecutionId
Every PublicSession has exactly one Execution owner
No global bare JSON-RPC request-id registry
No cancel-all behavior masquerading as task_control(cancel)
No single current_command used as multi-execution truth
No manually synchronized duplicate Permission/Workspace truths
No MCP Transport ownership of domain lifecycle
Structured filesystem and shell execution use distinct policy models
Update checking has a bounded typed lifecycle and cannot block startup
